title: Paid Media Agency Zurich: Google, LinkedIn, Meta | 22 Signals
description: Paid media for Zurich companies: Google, LinkedIn, Meta and YouTube campaigns split by language region, measured on qualified enquiries rather than clicks.
h1: A paid media agency for Zurich firms where every click is expensive
intro: We plan and run Google, LinkedIn, Meta and YouTube campaigns for Zurich companies that sell in a small, wealthy and multilingual market. Campaigns are split by language region, tracked to qualified enquiries and sales, and set up within Swiss advertising and data rules. You get a written plan in 5 to 7 days and a monthly report that shows what each franc returned.

sections.h: Why Swiss paid media needs a different setup
p: Switzerland combines a small population with high incomes and four languages. Audiences run out quickly, competition for valuable searches is strong and clicks in financial, legal and B2B categories are often expensive. A campaign copied from a German or UK playbook usually wastes money in the first weeks, because it targets too broadly and treats the country as one audience.

Language matters as much as location. Someone in Zurich may search in English, a client in Geneva in French, a prospect in Lugano in Italian. We build campaigns around language and region together, so each ad, keyword list and landing page speaks to the person seeing it.

LinkedIn Ads: precise B2B targeting by industry, seniority and company, valuable for finance, insurance and technology sales
Meta Ads: Facebook and Instagram for consumer brands, clinics, property and recruitment

Retargeting across channels, with frequency limits so ads stay useful rather than annoying
Landing pages built and tested by the same team, in each language you advertise in

p: In a market where one client can be worth a great deal, the number that matters is qualified enquiries and the business they turn into, not clicks or impressions. We connect ad platforms to your CRM or booking system, agree what counts as a qualified lead with your sales team and optimise campaigns against that.

Tracking has to respect the revised FADP, and GDPR for visitors from the EU. We set up consent banners and measurement that work within those rules, use server-side tagging where it helps, and are honest about what can and cannot be measured once people decline cookies.

Swiss advertising must be accurate and fair under the Unfair Competition Act, and the Swiss Commission for Fairness handles complaints about misleading ads. Financial firms face extra rules on how financial services and products are advertised, and health and pharmaceutical advertising has strict limits of its own.

We write ads and landing pages with those rules in mind and route anything sensitive to your compliance team before launch. The platforms add their own policies on financial services, health and personal attributes, and we keep accounts in good standing. We are not your lawyers, but we will flag risk early.

sections.h: Planning budgets around the Swiss calendar
p: Demand in Switzerland moves with the calendar. School holidays differ from canton to canton, many decision makers are away for parts of July and August, and the weeks before Christmas are busy for consumer brands and quiet for many B2B buyers. We plan budget phasing around those patterns, test early in the year when competition is lower in some sectors, and hold spend back when the data says buyers are not there.

Weak creative wastes budget faster than weak targeting. Because our team also produces video, motion graphics, AI video, animation and 3D renders, we can make ads that fit each channel, test several versions and refresh them before performance drops. For multilingual campaigns, copy in German, French or Italian comes from your team or localisation partners we arrange, and we adapt the visuals to match.

We are registered in London, one hour behind Zurich, and run campaigns remotely. Reviews and reporting calls happen in Swiss working hours. Your ad accounts stay in your name, and you pay the platforms directly, so you always own your data and history.

faqs.q: How much should a Zurich company spend on ads?
faqs.a: It depends on how competitive your searches are, how valuable a client is and how many languages you target. We recommend a starting budget in the written plan, based on expected costs and the number of enquiries you need, then adjust once real data arrives. Ad spend is paid to the platforms directly.

faqs.q: Should we advertise in English or German?
faqs.a: Often both, and sometimes French and Italian too. It depends on who your buyers are. International clients and many professionals in Zurich respond to English, while most consumers expect their own language. We split campaigns by language so results show which approach works.

faqs.q: Is LinkedIn worth it for Swiss B2B?
faqs.a: For finance, insurance, technology and professional services, it is often the most precise way to reach decision makers by role and company. Clicks cost more than on other channels, so we keep targeting tight, use strong offers and measure qualified leads rather than clicks.

faqs.q: What does a paid media agency Zurich firms hire need to report?
faqs.a: Spend, qualified leads and cost per qualified lead by channel and language, plus revenue where your CRM allows. Each report explains what changed, why and what we will test next. You also keep direct access to every ad account.

faqs.q: Can you advertise financial services in Switzerland?
faqs.a: Yes, within Swiss rules and platform policies. Financial advertising must be accurate, balanced and clear about risks, and some products have extra requirements. We draft with that in mind and your compliance team approves sensitive ads before launch.

faqs.q: Do we keep ownership of the ad accounts?
faqs.a: Yes. Accounts are set up in your name or transferred to you, and you pay the platforms directly. We work with access you grant, so if we part ways, your data, audiences and history stay with you.
